hypothesis.title: A second replay-parent ring keyed on a post-fault operation invoked at a never-restarted server with two stranded fault-crossing records addressed to it, cut at the invocation, served with the parent's arm set to a salted half of the plan-only slots
hypothesis.description: New parent SOURCE beside the merged ghost-signal corpus, same machinery, different signal, own ring, own slots. SIGNAL (read once per run, in path.rs invoke_client_request before schedule_client_op draws the request's priority, so the cut precedes every post-cut draw): at the invocation of a client operation with target t, (a) state.incarnation_at(t) == 0 and send_ledger[t].crash_pending == 0 (the target never restarted and has no queued crash), (b) at least two servers have incarnation > 0 (the invocation is after the second restart), (c) the network queue holds at least two records addressed to t from remote origins for which state.fault_crossing(origin, origin_incarnation) is true, from at least two distinct origins (two stranded records of dead incarnations converge on the survivor). The first invocation satisfying (a)-(c) sets state.write_cut = Some(ReplayCut{step, tape_pos: rng.position()}) (new field beside replay_cut on State, excluded from signature()) and bumps util_stats replay.write_ring.signal_runs. RING: GridArm gets write_corpus: Corpus<SingleRunConfig> (replay_corpus::Corpus reused unchanged, CAPACITY 64, CHILDREN_PER_PARENT 8, per arm as the ghost ring is); a fresh grid run whose RunResult carries write_cut is admitted with tape[..tape_pos] exactly as campaign.rs admits ghost parents; Seed gains arms: ArmSet and parent_run_id: i64. SLOTS: replay_corpus::is_write_slot(run_id) = is_slot && !is_prefix && salted_phase(run_id, WRITE_SALT, 2) == 1, i.e. a salted half of the plan-only slots (about 73,000 runs per chunk, 0.096 of runs); in GridArm::assign a write slot takes write_corpus.next_child() and, when that ring is empty, falls through to the ghost ring's plan-only child as today (counted replay.write_ring.slots_unfilled). CHILD: run_single_simulation::<F, ReplayRng> with the parent's tape, workload seed and config, and the child's run-id-keyed mechanism draws (ArmSet::coins, stall_cap, ghost_release cell, crash placement, timer context) evaluated under parent_run_id, as the iteration-28 inheritance did (research/lite/state/replay-prefix-inherit-parent-bits.json: fidelity 1.056 inherited against 0.322 own-id; its record says any future corpus that means 'replay this prefix' must inherit them); the child is never admitted to either ring and never feeds arm_selector::observe. BIT: WRITE_RING_SLOT = 1 << 26 in run_variant.rs joined by grid_arm_bits like REPLAY_SLOT (pure function of the id; carried whether or not the ring held a parent), row 67108864 in VARIANT_BITS renamed from the retired originAlternate to writeRingSlot. The child's tag also carries REPLAY_SLOT and the parent's inherited mechanism bits, and not REPLAY_PREFIX, so the grader's matched control is the other half of the plan-only ghost children. COUNTERS (util_stats.rs ReplayStats gains a write_ring block): signal_runs, parents_admitted, children, slots_unfilled, prefix_faithful (child fired the signal at the parent's cut step), children_signal_fired, cut_step_sum, child_steps_sum, control_plan_only_steps_sum. No config field; general_vr.json untouched.

hypothesis.rationale: The fresh cache (63a21f95fdfb seed 1000, 757,560 runs) reaches depth>=10 on 423 runs and depth>=11 on 59; the 10-to-11 conversion is 0.14 overall and, split by run class, fresh grid runs convert 24/108 = 0.22, plan-only ghost children 9/118 = 0.076, prefix ghost children 5/121 = 0.04, AOS 21/76 = 0.28. Only fresh runs are admitted as parents, and 108 fresh runs per chunk stand at the label-10 state with a recorded tape; today each of them is one trial at that state. The signal is what the oracle guarantees at label 10 in generic classes: w2 precedes deliver_svc_1_to_0 and deliver_svc_2_to_0 in the DAG, so at the write's invocation two records from two dead incarnations are undelivered to node 0, which never restarted, after recover_nl and recover_2. Every label-10 run therefore fires the signal (unless its plan still queues a crash of node 0, which would end the survivor's role anyway), and the signal is looser than the label: a post-fault invocation at a never-restarted target with two stranded ghosts from two origins. Supply grounding: runs with two recovered nodes are 535,949 of 757,560 (0.71), post-fault invocations 2,263,203 per chunk (client_anchor.census treated 1,567,477 + control 695,726), stale deliveries 4,125,894 per chunk (delivery_effects.sender_restarted), so conditions (a)-(b) are common and (c) at one target from two origins is the selective clause; the expected signal share of the 329,087 fresh grid runs is 0.01-0.15 (3,300-50,000 parents per chunk against a serving rate of about 73,000 children per chunk, i.e. 1.5-8 children per parent before the 64-ring displaces it). Expected yield at the honest rung: 108 label-10 parents x 1.5-8 children x fidelity 0.7-0.9 x conversion 0.14-0.22 = 16-150 additional depth>=11 events per chunk on a treated share whose baseline expectation is 73,000 x 0.062/1,000 = 4.5, against 59 per chunk in the whole cache. The 8-10 rungs inflate mechanically because a faithful child replays its parent's prefix past them (the ghost ring was merged on exactly this at depth>=6, 2.19x); depth>=11 is never replayed since the cut precedes it, so it is the read that measures search. The prior deep-cut closure (replay-tier-answered-overtake-cut, depth>=8 per run 0.645) had 332,289 tier-2 parents per session, half of all fresh runs, so its children replayed unenriched prefixes to a finished state; this signal is 5-50x tighter and the applicability clause below refutes the mechanism if it is not.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: Stated entirely in the simulator's own event classes: a client operation invocation, the target's incarnation count and queued-crash count, the count of restarted nodes, and records in the network queue whose sending incarnation is dead (state.fault_crossing). No handler, message, role or timer label is named. On any protocol the state 'stale records from two dead incarnations still addressed to a survivor when a client operation reaches it' is the generic shape of a recovery-versus-client race; on protocols without restarts the signal never fires, the ring stays empty and the write slots run as plan-only ghost children, so the panel's clean specs and other bugs see no change beyond a half of the plan-only attribution arm being re-purposed.

nestedHypothesis.title: Adaptive switch at the checkpoint: a write-ring child that reaches its cut with the signal still true runs its suffix under the uniform within-queue selector so the order among records already in flight is re-drawn per child instead of fixed by the prefix's priorities
nestedHypothesis.description: Nested cell of write-region-replay-ring. The within-queue selector is built once per run in path.rs (queue_policy.to_selector(), within_queue_selector) and threaded to select_within_queue; on a treated write-ring child, at the step where the replay reaches the parent's cut_step and state.write_cut is set at that step (the signal reproduced), path.rs swaps the within-queue selector from the config's Tournament{k:10} to Proportional{exponent: 0.0} (uniform over eligible items, an existing built selector) for the remainder of the run; a child whose replay did not reproduce the signal keeps the tournament (counted replay.write_ring.uniform.not_switched). The queue policy (local/network/timer) is untouched. BIT: WRITE_RING_UNIFORM_SUFFIX = 1 << 29 (row 536870912 renamed from the retired pairOrderGhostOnly to writeRingUniformSuffix), a salted half of the write slots, implies WRITE_RING_SLOT. COUNTERS: replay.write_ring.uniform.switched, not_switched, and for both halves of the ring first_post_cut_delivery_at_target.{stale, fresh, total} (the class of the first record delivered to the cut operation's target after the cut). No config field.
buildsOn: record priority draws (state.rs sample, Beta(0.5,0.5) band)
nestedHypothesis.rationale: Under the config's Tournament{k:10} with steer terms at zero the score of a record is its priority drawn once at send time from the band 0.5 +- 0.15 x Beta(0.5, 0.5) (steer_terms.rs), and with a handful of eligible records the tournament is near-greedy on that draw. Every record already in flight at the cut carries a priority drawn in the prefix, identical in every child of the parent; and the records that matter past the write survived undelivered through the prefix precisely because their draws were low. The oracle's 10-to-11 transition needs two records that were in flight before the write (the recovery replies to the second-restarted node) delivered before the record the write causes (the replication record), which under the tournament is the chance that one fresh draw lands below two survivor draws that are low by selection - the cache reads this conversion at 0.14 (59/423) and 0.22 on fresh runs; under uniform selection the ordering of three eligible records is exchangeable and the same event has probability about 1/3. The 11-to-12 transition (the reply from the restarted node's current incarnation delivered to the never-restarted node before the two dead-incarnation records that survived there) is favoured by the tournament for the same reason (0.68 in the cache) and falls toward 1/3-0.45 under uniform selection, so the honest expectation over both is a small net gain with the loss moved from 11 to 12, and depth>=12 is recorded to see it. The directive's own version of this cell - re-drawing the fresh-first and pair-order bits per child - is inert on these transitions: fresh_first_dispatch returns the drawn ghost at a destination whose incarnation is 0 (scheduler.rs, record_fresh_first_skipped_never_restarted_dest), and pair_order acts only between records of one sender to one destination sent by the same incarnation, while the records contending here are from different senders.
nestedHypothesis.generalityArgument: The switch is between two built, protocol-agnostic within-queue selectors, keyed on a generic run event (the replay reached its checkpoint with the checkpoint's signal reproduced). It expresses no preference among record classes; it removes a preference the prefix fixed. On a protocol where the ring is empty it never fires.

nestedHypothesis.redTeam: The band identifies the cache's 10->11 conversion (0.14-0.22) with the ordering probability of three records at one target, but the conversion also carries the acted requirement, the exclusion of N1's later sends and the plan's shape, so uniform selection cannot lift it to 1/3; the 11->12 transition moves the other way by the candidate's own account, so the net over the two may be zero. Uniform selection over ALL eligible records for the whole suffix also re-randomizes every other destination, not only the target, which adds noise the tournament's near-greedy order did not have; and the suffix under Proportional{0} is a different explorer whose depth-8 rates are unmeasured on this template. The write-region replay ring (7-0) leads: the DAG guarantee for its signal verified (w2 -> deliver_svc_1_to_0 and w2 -> deliver_svc_2_to_0, both dead-incarnation direct-RPC records to the never-restarted node 0 after both restarts), every cache figure re-derived from the merged-tree baseline (class counts 329,087/145,760/145,193/137,520; depth>=10 by class 108/121/118/76 and depth>=11 24/5/9/21 computed by joining metrics.variants rows on REPLAY_SLOT, REPLAY_PREFIX, PROBE and the arm mode; ladder 13372/2674/423/59/40/15; 535,949 two-recovered runs; 2,263,203 post-fault invocations; 4,125,894 stale deliveries; ring 91,926 / 274,268 / 75,386 of 137,527 / 16,685), and the source claims (generic Corpus, rng.position, the cut before the request's priority draw, replay_cut outside signature). It is a new parent source with its own ring, not a retired ranking rule. One design gap found and fixed by rewrite: inheriting the parent's mechanism draws (required for fidelity, iteration 28) tags children with the parents' bits, so the grader's co-bit balance check will blank the internal primary; the session reads the contrast stratified over the inherited strata as at iteration 28. How the session reads the ring: treated = write slots (1<<26, half of the plan-only slots, 0.096 of runs), control = the other plan-only half (ghost-ring plan-only children, 4.5-7.5 depth-11 events expected per chunk); depth 8-10 are mechanical replay and are guards only; the honest rung is depth>=11 per run (never replayed by the DAG), band [2.0, 40] pooled over two chunks with sibling inflation, met on an inflated lower edge above 1.5 (about 60 treated against 12 control events), with cross-binary depth>=8 per second [0.95, 1.12] and a stratified depth>=8 per run at or above 0.9 as the merge guards. Second bit: the uniform-suffix cell (5-0, 1<<29) pairs with the ring this session - cost 0, control the tournament half of the same ring, a chunk-1 observable (stale-first share at the target) on thousands of events, and it tests the one thing a tape checkpoint cannot vary (the order among records already in flight); its depth>=11 band is a lean at 8-75 events per half. The state fork (4-2) waits: history verified whole in the filed patch and clone wall negligible, but cost 2 by the rubric and precedent and a per-second gain inside the floor on a 0.048 share. The second-generation admission (2-0) is not gradable: 0.024 share is below TREATED_SHARE_MIN 0.05 and a floor of 100 children gives no read; a follow-up once the ring's marker-free counters price its supply. Rejected: replay-parent-served-by-child-arm-set as a retired 'which parent a slot is served' ranking rule; pulled-crash-waits as parentless on the merged tree (the restart pull closed at 79 and restart_pull does not exist in spur 12b7582).
